items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 198:1
items.html: In the world of Beriah there are three aspects: food, covering, and conjugal rights. But in Yetzirah there is no aspect of conjugal rights, for conjugal rights means a coupling to beget offspring, and therefore in Beriah, where there are the Mochin of the GAR of Ima, there is a coupling to beget souls for the angels of Yetzirah. But in Yetzirah itself, where there are no GAR, there is no conjugal rights, but only food and covering alone, that is, only a coupling to sustain the worlds, and not to beget souls. And this is called food. And this coupling, to sustain the worlds, is also practiced in the world of Assiyah. Only the aspect of the covering, which is the aspect of a cover before the externals, is not practiced there toward itself, for it itself, in its entirety, is the aspect of a covering over the world of Yetzirah. (Items 132 to 138).
